1

This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of MV Act, praying to enhance the compensation amount payables to him by suitably modifying the judgment and award dated 03-03- 2018 passed by the learned II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT Kalaburagi in MVC No.170/2017, in the interest of justice and equity.
This appeal coming on for Final Hearing, through physical hearing/video conference, this day T.G.Shivashankare Gowda, J., delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the appellant has challenged the judgment dated 03.03.2018 passed in M.V.C.No.170/2017 on the file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).
2. The appellant was the petitioner, the respondents were the respondents before the Tribunal.
The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Briefly stated, the facts are that, the petitioner has suffered severe shoulder injury in a road accident that took place on 21-02-2017 near Keshavareddy School on Mannaguda Parigi road, Pudur Mandal while he was travelling as a passenger in the bus bearing registration No.KA-32/C-0191 from Hyderabad to Kalaburgi, which turned turtle on the road.
The right elbow of the petitioner was amputated for which he was hospitalized for 4 days.

He claimed compensation of Rs.98,75,000/-
pleading that he was aged 32 years, working as a Mechanical Engineer in Tengali Marketing,
Kalaburagi and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.8,69,200/- with 6% interest.
4. The petitioner has pleaded inadequacy in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

According to him, income taken at Rs.6,000/- is on the lower side, inspite of 90% of whole body disability suffered by him, Tribunal has taken only 30%, loss of amenities, pain and sufferings was ignored and lesser compensation has been awarded under different heads and sought for enhancement.
5.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the injured was earning Rs.18,000/- per month being a Mechanical Engineer and as employee of Tengli Marketing, Kalaburagi, medical evidence assessed 90% whole body disability, pecuniary and non-pecuniary heads were not considered with proportion to the gravity of the injury, and accordingly he sought for re- assessment and enhancement.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company though supported the impugned judgment contended that percentage of disability is correctly assessed, correct income was taken by the Tribunal, amount granted towards pain and sufferings and loss of disability is correct, and a nominal enhancement may be granted under different heads.

sentences.text: We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.

8. As seen from the impugned judgment, there is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident;
the petitioner was the passenger of the bus, injury sustained by the petitioner on account of accident and his entitlement to claim the compensation.

It is noticed that the Tribunal has considered that the petitioner is a passport holder, Mechanical Engineer and taken income at Rs.10,000/-, assessed whole body disability at 30%, awarded Rs.20,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.2,000/-
towards attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance, Rs.2,000/- towards loss of income during laid up, Rs.5,76,000/- towards loss of income due to disability and Rs.10,000/-
towards loss of amenities and nutrition food, Rs.59,700/- towards medical expenses and Rs.1,99,500/- towards cost of the elbow prosthesis.

9. The medical records, such as, Ex.P.8/ discharge summery, Exs.P9 to P16/medical records and Ex.P24/disability certificate along with evidence of PW.2 Dr.Ramakant Kulkarni, point out that due to fracture of right shoulder, the right elbow was amputated resulting in 90% whole body disability.
PW.2 is though a non- treating doctor, the amputation injury is schedule injury under Workmen's Compensation Act, which needs any expert opinion for assessment of disability.
Therefore, the assessment of whole body disability of 30% by the Tribunal has no rationale.

Even in the absence of medical evidence, the Tribunal can assess the percentage of disability with reference to schedule at 85% whole body disability, if the amputation is upper 1/3rd of the shoulder.
Hence, we assess the whole body disability at 85%.
As mentioned above, the compensation assessed by the Tribunal under different heads is on the lower side and not proportionate to the gravity and nature of the injury and it needs modification.
10. For determining the amount of compensation for loss of income, the relevant factor, is the age and income of the injured.

The petitioner has relied upon the Ex.P18 to 21, the certificate of training,
employment letter, and salary certificate and termination letter.
The Tribunal has discussed that there is no proof of salary being credited to the bank account of the petitioner and declined to accept it.
If the petitioner is on a permanent employment, he has to be assigned with provident fund account number, profession tax has to be deducted and paid to the Government.
In the absence of this procedure being followed, Exs.P18 to 21 will not inspire the confidence of the Court.

For those who have no proof of income, for the accident of 2017, the notional income is not less than Rs.10,250/-, hence, the income of the petitioner is assessed accordingly for that relevant point of time and his age was admittedly 32.
11. By applying the principles laid down in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680, future prospects should be taken as 40% for age below 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
For the age of petitioner 32, applicable multiplier in view of the principles laid down in Sarla Verma v. DTC- (2009)6 SCC 121, is '16'.
12.

If all these factors are taken into consideration, the assessment of compensation to the injured is:
Towards 1. Pain and Suffering Rs.1,00,000/-,

3 2. Loss of Amenities and discomforts Rs.1,00,000/-, 3. Medical expenses of Rs.59,700/-, 4.
Attendant and conveyance charges Rs.20,000/-, 5. Food and Nourishment Rs.10,000/-, 6. Loss of income during laid up for 6months Rs.61,500/-, 7. Loss of income due to disability at Rs.23,41,920/-(10,250/-+4,100(40% future prospects) =14,350 x 12 x 16 x 85%) and 8. Expenses towards elbow prosthesis Rs.1,99,500/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In all, the petitioner is entitled to Rs.28,92,620/- as against Rs.8,69,200/-, thereby there shall be an enhancement of Rs.20,23,420/-.
The appeal filed by the petitioner deserves to be allowed accordingly.

13. In the result, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
The petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.28,92,620/- as against Rs.8,69,200/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact.
The 2nd respondent/Insurance Company is directed to satisfy the award within 8weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Office is directed to transfer the amount if any in deposit, to the Tribunal, forthwith.
